tweets: Adalaj Vav, Gujarat, 1498 — a five-storey stepwell sunk deep into the earth, its shaded galleries running several degrees cooler than the blazing surface above: an early triumph of passive cooling, engineered straight into stone.

Each landing bears carved lotus friezes and pierced stone screens; the well doubled as a cool gathering place through Gujarat's fierce summers, when villagers came for water, shade and rest. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
